Soundscape describes the world around you with sound. You hear each place from the direction it is in, so you learn where things are as well as what they are.
As you walk, Soundscape calls out streets, intersections and places near you. You do not need to do anything. See the *Automatic Callouts* help page.
The four buttons at the bottom of the home screen describe your surroundings whenever you ask. They are *My Location*, *Around Me*, *Ahead of Me* and *Nearby Markers*.
An audio beacon is a sound that plays from the direction of a place you choose. It shows you where the place is, and you decide how to get there. See the *Audio Beacon* help page.

While you walk, Soundscape uses your direction of travel, so your phone can stay in a pocket or bag. When you stand still, point the top of your phone the way you are facing. Soundscape then uses your phone as a compass. If your phone is locked, or Soundscape is not on the screen, hold your phone flat as well.
Stereo headphones give the clearest sense of direction. Soundscape also works through your phone's speaker.
To try the main features step by step, open the menu and select *Guided tutorial*.

Soundscape can use any voice installed on your phone. To add voices, open your phone's settings and find *Text-to-speech output*. To choose a voice in Soundscape, open the menu and select *Settings*, then *Audio*, then *Voices*.
Soundscape normally downloads map data as you move. Without an internet connection it cannot do that. To keep everything working, download an offline map before you travel.

1. Open the menu and select *Offline maps*.

2. Select a map from *Nearby offline maps*.

3. Select *Download offline map*.

Maps can be large, so use Wi-Fi if you can.

Callouts may still work in places you visited recently, because your phone keeps some map data for a while. Search finds only your markers. Everything returns to normal when your phone is back online.
Your use of Soundscape is subject to the terms of the %1$s and the terms set out below (together, the *“Terms of Use”*).

You acknowledge that Soundscape (1) is not designed, intended, or made available as a medical device, and (2) is not designed or intended to be a substitute for professional medical advice, diagnosis, treatment, or judgement and should not be used to replace or as a substitute for professional medical advice, diagnosis, treatment, or judgement.

Safety Notice

Soundscape is a navigation aid and should not be used in lieu of mobility skills, being aware of your surroundings, and good judgement. Use caution when navigating your environment as the mapping data incorporated into the Soundscape program is captured from a third-party program, and therefore, there may be limitations with the accuracy of the information presented.

Soundscape needs certain permissions to run. These permissions let the app receive your phone's location, even when the phone is locked. Please tap each of the following permissions and turn them on when prompted:
When navigating with Soundscape, you will hear the audio beacon in the direction of your destination. By following its sound, you will always know which way to go.
Listen to the available audio beacons and select your preference.
This can be changed later in app settings.
You are ready for your first walk with Soundscape. To get started, choose a nearby destination and start the audio beacon — you’ll hear it playing in the direction of your destination.

An audio beacon is a sound that plays from the direction of a place you choose. It tells you where the place is in a straight line. It does not give turn-by-turn directions, so you choose your own way there.
The beacon changes sound when you face the place or walk straight towards it. To find that sound, hold your phone flat and turn slowly. You can choose a different beacon sound in *Settings*.

1. Find the place. Use the search bar, *Places Nearby*, *Markers* or *Current Location* on the home screen.

2. Select the place to open *Location Details*.

3. Select *Start Audio Beacon*.

Soundscape returns to the home screen and the beacon starts. The home screen shows the name of the place and how far away it is.
Select *Stop Route* on the home screen. The button has this name even when the beacon is not part of a route.
Select *Mute Beacon* on the home screen. Soundscape still tells you how far away the place is as you move. Select *Unmute Beacon* to hear the beacon again.

When you are about 12 metres from the place, Soundscape tells you and removes the beacon. Your phone cannot find your position more exactly than that. To hear the beacon again, set it again.\n\nA beacon set on a place less than 30 metres away stays on until you remove it.
As you walk, Soundscape calls out what is near you. You hear each name from the direction of the place. Callouts cover streets, intersections, shops, bus stops, landmarks and your own markers.
As you approach an intersection, Soundscape names each road that leaves it. You hear which road goes left, which continues ahead and which goes right.

Open the menu and select *Settings*, then *Manage Callouts*. *Callout Detail* has four levels.

*Detailed* calls out everything nearby.

*Simplified* leaves out minor paths and service roads, and repeats itself less.

*Essential* calls out only streets, intersections and landmarks.

*Silent* makes no automatic callouts. Beacons, routes and the home screen buttons still work.

*Manage Callouts* has two more settings. *Streets and Junctions* turns street and intersection callouts on or off. *Places to Call Out* chooses which kinds of place you hear, such as *Public Transport* or *Food and Drink*. Your markers are always called out.

Press *previous* on your headphone controls. Each press moves one level quieter: *Detailed*, *Simplified*, *Essential*, then *Silent*. One more press returns to *Detailed*. See the *Using Media Controls* help page.

Select the *Sleep* button at the top of the home screen. Soundscape stops using your location and makes no sound until you select *Wake Up Now*. Or select *Wake On Leave*, and Soundscape wakes up when you leave the place you are in.

Soundscape notices when you are travelling at vehicle speed. It then stops calling out intersections and nearby shops, because they pass too quickly. Instead it calls out the road you are on, landmarks, stops and stations, rivers and tunnels.
In a Vehicle or on a Train
*My Location* tells you where you are. It says which way you are facing or travelling, then the street or address you are at. Use it when you step off a bus, leave a building or lose your bearings.

*Nearby Markers* calls out up to four of your markers, the ones closest to you. You hear each one from its own direction, with its distance. Use it to get your bearings from places you already know. Markers more than about 2 kilometres away are left out.

*Around Me* calls out up to four places near you: one ahead, one to the right, one behind and one to the left. You hear each one from its own direction, with its distance. Use it to get your bearings when you arrive somewhere.
*Ahead of Me* calls out up to five places in front of you. You hear each one from its own direction, with its distance. Use it on a street you do not know, to learn what is coming up.
If you are standing still, first point the top of your phone the way you are facing. If your phone is locked, or Soundscape is not on the screen, hold your phone flat as well.

You can control Soundscape with the media buttons on your headphones: *play/pause*, *next* and *previous*. This works with wired and Bluetooth headphones. It also works when Soundscape is in the background or your phone is locked.\n\nNot all headphones have all three buttons.
The buttons only control Soundscape when no other app is playing audio. If you are playing music or a podcast, the buttons control that app instead.

The buttons only control Soundscape when no other app is playing audio. If you are playing music or a podcast, the buttons control that app instead.\n\nThe buttons also do not control Soundscape while *Mix audio with other apps* is turned on in *Settings*.
The buttons can work in two ways: *Original mode* or *Audio menu*. To choose, open the menu and select *Settings*, then *Media Controls*.

*Play/pause* mutes the beacon. Press it again to hear the beacon.

*Next* moves the beacon to the next waypoint when you are following a route. Otherwise it calls out *Around Me*.

*Previous* moves the beacon to the previous waypoint when you are following a route. Otherwise it changes the *Callout Detail*. Each press moves one level quieter: *Detailed*, *Simplified*, *Essential*, then *Silent*. One more press returns to *Detailed*. Soundscape says the name of the new level.

The audio menu gives you more actions from the same three buttons. Soundscape reads each option aloud.

*Next* moves to the next option. After the last option it returns to the first.

*Play/pause* selects the option you just heard.

*Previous* changes the *Callout Detail*, the same as in *Original mode*.

The menu starts with four groups: *Hear My Surroundings*, *Route control*, *Start Route* and *Start Audio Beacon*. Select a group to hear its actions. *Hear My Surroundings* and *Route control* end with *Top menu*, which takes you back to the four groups.
A marker is a place you have saved. It can be any place that matters to you: your home, a bus stop, a building entrance or a crossing.
Soundscape calls out your markers as you pass them. You can set an audio beacon on a marker, add it to a route, or hear the closest ones with the *Nearby Markers* button.

1. Select *Markers* on the home screen, then select *New*.

2. Choose *Current Location*, or a place from *Places Nearby*.

3. Change the name if you want, and add notes. Soundscape reads the notes out with the marker.

4. Select *Done*.
You can also save any place you find. Open its *Location Details* and select *Save as Marker*.
Select the marker on the *Markers* screen, then select *Edit Marker*. You can change its name, notes and position, or select *Delete Marker*. Deleting a marker also removes it from your routes.
A route is a list of locations, called waypoints, that you visit in order. Soundscape sets a beacon on the first waypoint. When you arrive, it tells you and moves the beacon to the next one.
Use a route to learn a new journey, or to stay on track on one you know.

1. Select *Routes* on the home screen, then select *New*.

2. Give the route a name. You can add a description.

3. Select *Add Waypoints* and choose markers. You can also add your current location or a place nearby.

4. Select *Done*.
Select the route on the *Routes* screen, then select *Edit Route*. You can add, remove and reorder waypoints, change the name and description, or delete the route.
Select the route on the *Routes* screen, then select *Share*.

Select the route on the *Routes* screen, then select *Start Route*. To follow it backwards, select *Start Route in Reverse*. On the home screen, *Next Waypoint* and *Previous Waypoint* move the beacon along the route. *Stop Route* ends it.

Use Soundscape whenever you are out. It runs in the background and tells you the streets you are on and the places you pass. It can also help with one task, such as keeping track of a place you are walking to.
How do I get the most out of a beacon?

Think of the beacon as a lighthouse for your ears. It shows where the place is in a straight line, not the path to it. You still choose your way around buildings and across roads.

The beacon changes sound when you face the place. To find that sound, hold your phone flat and turn slowly.

If you know most of the way, mute the beacon and unmute it when you are close.
Why does the beacon sound different when I stop walking?

With your phone in a pocket or bag, Soundscape works out which way you face from your direction of travel. When you stop, it can no longer tell, so the beacon plays as if you were facing away. Start walking again, or point the top of your phone the way you are facing. If your phone is locked, or Soundscape is not on the screen, hold your phone flat as well.
Can I set a beacon on an address, such as my home?
Yes. Type the address in the search bar on the home screen and select it in the results. Then select *Start Audio Beacon*. To keep the address for next time, select *Save as Marker*.
What happens when I reach my destination?

When you are about 12 metres away, Soundscape tells you and removes the beacon. Your phone cannot find your position more exactly than that, so use your other skills for the last few steps. To hear the beacon again, set it again.
Why do I hear a road name twice at an intersection?

Soundscape names each road that leaves the intersection, from the direction it goes. A road that crosses yours goes both left and right, so you hear its name twice. If you hear only a left and a right, your road ends ahead.
Why doesn’t Soundscape announce every business that I pass?

Soundscape gets its places from OpenStreetMap, a map built by volunteers. If a business is missing from that map, Soundscape cannot call it out. Soundscape also limits callouts so that you do not hear too many. To hear more, set *Callout Detail* to *Detailed* and check *Places to Call Out*.
What changes when I am in a vehicle?
Soundscape stops calling out intersections and nearby shops, because they pass too quickly. Instead it calls out the road you are on, landmarks, stops and stations, rivers and tunnels.
What if I miss a callout?
Soundscape does not keep a list of past callouts. Ask again with the buttons at the bottom of the home screen: *My Location*, *Around Me* or *Ahead of Me*.
What phone does Soundscape run on?
Soundscape runs on iPhones with iOS 16 or later, and on Android phones with Android 11 or later.
No. Soundscape works through your phone's speaker. Stereo headphones give a much clearer sense of direction, and any wired or Bluetooth pair will do.

Soundscape uses your location all the time, and that uses battery. To use less:

1. Keep the screen off when you are not using it.

2. When you stop for a while, select *Sleep* at the top of the home screen. Select *Wake On Leave* if you want Soundscape to wake when you move on.

3. When you have finished, close Soundscape.
How much mobile data does Soundscape use?
Soundscape downloads a small amount of map data as you move. To use much less, download an offline map over Wi-Fi before you travel. Open the menu and select *Offline maps*.
How is Soundscape different from other map apps?

Most map apps give turn-by-turn directions. Soundscape tells you what is around you and plays a beacon from the direction of your destination. You choose the way.\n\nYou can use both together. Start directions in your map app, then set a Soundscape beacon on the same place.
How do I make Soundscape quieter?

1. To hear fewer callouts, open *Settings*, select *Manage Callouts* and lower *Callout Detail*. *Silent* stops all automatic callouts.

2. To silence the beacon, select *Mute Beacon* on the home screen.

3. To stop Soundscape for a while, select *Sleep* at the top of the home screen.
Do I need to hold my phone all the time?

No. While you walk, Soundscape uses your direction of travel, so your phone can stay in a pocket or bag. Take it out when you are standing still and want directions to be right. Point the top of your phone the way you are facing. If your phone is locked, or Soundscape is not on the screen, hold your phone flat as well.

OpenStreetMap is a free map of the world, built by volunteers. Soundscape uses it for streets and places. Anyone can add or correct a place at www.openstreetmap.org, and the change reaches Soundscape in a later map update.
To find nearby bus stops, select *Places Nearby* and choose *Public Transport*.
You can mute the beacon and still hear how far away the place is. Soundscape says the distance from time to time as you move.
If you take the same bus often, save your stops as markers. Set a beacon on the stop where you get off, and Soundscape tells you how far away it is as you ride.
To explore a place before you go, open its *Location Details* and select *Simulate Location*. Soundscape then behaves as if you were there.
For turn-by-turn directions, open the *Location Details* of a place and select *Open in Maps App*. Soundscape keeps running while the other app gives directions.
The Soundscape location service runs even when the phone is locked.

Welcome to the guided tutorial. This tutorial will guide you through the main features of the app. You can stop the tutorial at any time by tapping Cancel Guided Tutorial in the Main Menu. Let's start with Places Nearby. It lets you find points of interest. The Places Nearby button is on the Home screen, just below the Search bar. Tap it now to try it.
Places Nearby groups points of interest by type. Browse the places in the lists and select one.

Great! You're now on the Location Details screen. From here you can save this location as a Marker, along with other actions. With Soundscape, you can mark any place that matters to you, such as your home, your bus stop, or even the spot where you are standing. Try it now. Save this location as a marker by tapping Save as Marker.
Great! When creating a marker, you can edit its name and add notes. Try that now, and when you're ready, tap Done.

Now that you know how to use Markers, let's look at some of the other features. At the bottom of the screen are four buttons. We'll try each one. The button on the left is My Location. It describes your current location. Try tapping it now.
The next button is Around Me. This tells you what’s nearby in each direction. Tap Around Me.
The next button is Ahead of Me. It tells you what’s in front of you. Tap Ahead of Me.
The final button is Nearby Markers, which announces saved places around you. Tap Nearby Markers to try it.
You have now successfully created a marker. Let's play an audio beacon to guide us to that location. Tap Markers, just below Places Nearby.
You’re now on the Markers screen, which lists all your saved markers. Select a marker, and when the Location Details screen appears tap Start Audio Beacon.
You can now hear the audio beacon. It plays from the direction of your destination. As you turn your phone, you can hear the beacon move and change how it sounds. Try it now.

When your phone is locked, the beacon will still play. If you are walking or in a vehicle, the app uses your direction of travel to play the audio beacon. However, even when your phone is locked, you can hold it flat in front of you, like a compass. Then the beacon uses the direction your phone is pointing. Try it now.
When you’re ready to stop the beacon, tap the Stop Route button.
That completes the tutorial. You can run it again from the main menu. We hope you find the app useful!

On iPhone, you can ask Siri to do things in Soundscape without touching your phone. For example, hear a callout, start a route, or set a beacon on a marker.\n\nSoundscape answers in its own voice, with its usual callouts and beacon sounds. So you still hear each sound from the direction of the place.

Use voice commands when your phone is in your pocket or your hands are full. They work while Soundscape is in the background and while your phone is locked. Asking for a callout does not open the app.\n\nSiri does the listening, not Soundscape. So Soundscape never uses your microphone, and your Bluetooth headphones keep their high quality sound.

Every command has the same shape: *“Soundscape”*, then a group, then your choice. For example, *“Soundscape surroundings around me”*.\n\nYou can also stop after the group, and Siri asks which choice you want. So each group works like a spoken menu. There are only seven groups to remember.

*“Soundscape surroundings”* — then *My Location*, *Around Me*, *Ahead of Me*, *Nearby Markers*, *Call out Beacon* or *Beacon Info*.

*“Soundscape route”* — then *Next Waypoint*, *Previous Waypoint*, *Mute Beacon* or *Stop*.

*“Soundscape start route”* — then the name of one of your routes.

*“Soundscape beacon”* — then the name of one of your markers.

*“Soundscape stop beacon”*.

*“Soundscape detail”* — then *Silent*, *Essential*, *Simplified* or *Detailed*. *Silent* turns automatic callouts off.

*“Soundscape list”* — then *Routes*, *Markers* or *Commands*. *Commands* reads this list back to you.
The commands also appear in the Shortcuts app, and in the iOS Settings app under *Siri*. There you can see the whole list and add your own wording for any command.

Callout detail controls how much Soundscape tells you about as you walk or travel. Detailed mode calls out everything nearby. Simplified mode leaves out minor paths and service roads, and repeats itself less often. Essential mode calls out streets, junctions and landmarks only, and when travelling by car or bus, only main and numbered roads, with no bus stops. Silent mode makes no automatic callouts at all, leaving beacons, routes and the buttons on the home screen.

Soundscape can only describe your surroundings as well as your phone knows where you are. Accuracy of 10 metres or better is good. Up to 20 metres is OK. Beyond that, callouts may name the wrong side of the street or arrive late.\n\nAccuracy is usually worst indoors, among tall buildings, and in the first minute after you go outside.
